stem: What should a technician do **first** before opening a computer's case?

options.content: Switch off and unplug the computer
options.rationale: Correct: never work inside a computer that is connected to the mains.

options.content: Remove the RAM modules
options.rationale: The computer must be switched off and unplugged before touching any component.

options.content: Run a disk-checking utility
options.rationale: That is a software check, not a safety step.

options.content: Open the power supply unit to check the fuse
options.rationale: The PSU must never be opened.

explanation: Safety first: switch off, unplug, discharge static, then open the case.

stem: What is the purpose of an **anti-static wrist strap**?

options.content: To stop static electricity from damaging components
options.rationale: Correct: it safely discharges static from the technician.

options.content: To protect the technician from mains electric shocks
options.rationale: The computer must be unplugged; the strap does not protect against mains voltage.

options.content: To hold small screws while working
options.rationale: It is not a tool holder.

options.content: To measure the temperature of the CPU
options.rationale: It does not measure anything.

explanation: Electrostatic discharge can destroy chips; the strap keeps the technician at the same potential as the case.

stem: Which part converts mains electricity into the low voltages used by a computer's components?

options.content: Motherboard
options.rationale: The motherboard connects the components; it receives power from the PSU.

options.content: Heat sink
options.rationale: A heat sink removes heat from the CPU.

options.content: Graphics card
options.rationale: A graphics card produces the display image.

options.content: Power supply unit (PSU)
options.rationale: Correct.

explanation: The PSU converts mains AC into the low DC voltages the components need.

stem: A wireless mouse's pointer has stopped moving. The receiver is plugged in. What should be checked first?

options.content: The amount of RAM installed
options.rationale: RAM does not affect whether a mouse moves the pointer.

options.content: The batteries in the mouse
options.rationale: Correct: flat batteries are the most common, simplest cause.

options.content: Whether the hard drive is clicking
options.rationale: A hard drive fault would not stop only the mouse.

options.content: The fan on the CPU heat sink
options.rationale: The CPU fan does not affect the mouse.

explanation: Check the simplest causes first: batteries, connection, surface, then drivers.

stem: A computer beeps several times at start-up and sometimes crashes with a blue error screen. Which component is the most likely cause?

options.content: A dirty mouse sensor
options.rationale: This would only affect the pointer.

options.content: A keyboard with a sticky key
options.rationale: This would only affect typing.

options.content: An out-of-date web browser
options.rationale: This would not cause POST beeps.

options.content: A faulty or loose RAM module
options.rationale: Correct: memory faults give POST beeps and random crashes.

explanation: Beep codes at POST and random crashes point to memory: reseat, test and if necessary replace the module.
hints: Which component is checked by the POST beeps and causes random crashes when faulty?

stem: An office computer's hard drive is making a clicking noise and some files will not open. What should be done **first**?

options.content: Defragment the hard drive
options.rationale: Heavy disk activity could make a failing drive fail sooner.

options.content: Install a new keyboard
options.rationale: The keyboard is not involved.

options.content: Back up the important files immediately
options.rationale: Correct: the drive may fail completely at any time.

options.content: Increase the screen brightness
options.rationale: The display is not involved.

explanation: Clicking and corrupted files are signs of a failing drive: back up first, then check and replace.
hints: What could be lost if the drive fails completely?

stem: Which task is an example of **preventive** maintenance?

options.content: Replacing a keyboard after coffee is spilled on it
options.rationale: That is repairing a fault after it happens.

options.content: Cleaning dust from fans and vents every term
options.rationale: Correct: it stops overheating before it causes a fault.

options.content: Reinstalling a program that keeps crashing
options.rationale: That fixes an existing fault.

options.content: Replacing a hard drive that has failed
options.rationale: That repairs a fault.

explanation: Preventive maintenance stops faults happening: cleaning, updates, backups, surge protection.

stem: Why should a technician test only **one** possible cause at a time when troubleshooting?

options.content: Because the computer can only be opened once a day
options.rationale: There is no such limit.

options.content: Because testing two things at once always damages the motherboard
options.rationale: Testing does not damage the motherboard.

options.content: So that it is clear which change fixed the fault
options.rationale: Correct: changing several things at once hides the real cause.

options.content: So that the fault log does not need to be completed
options.rationale: The fault should still be recorded.

explanation: One change at a time identifies the true cause, which helps fix similar faults in future.
hints: If several things are changed at once, how will you know what fixed the fault?

stem: It is safe to open a computer's power supply unit once the computer has been unplugged.
explanation: False. The PSU (and monitors) can hold dangerous charges even when unplugged; they should never be opened.

stem: Components such as RAM modules should be held by their edges, not by their gold contacts.
explanation: True. Touching the contacts or chips can leave dirt or cause static damage.

stem: Match each symptom to the most suitable first action.

left.content: Pointer jumps about on a glass desk
A program has frozen and will not respond
"No boot device" message after the computer was moved
Typed characters appear as different symbols

right.content: Check the drive's data and power cables
Use a mouse mat and clean the sensor
Close it using Task Manager and restart it

explanation: Match the symptom to its most likely cause and try the simplest fix first.
hints: Link each symptom to the component involved, then the fix.

stem: Match each part of a PC to its purpose.

right.content: Holds programs and data currently in use
Main circuit board connecting all components

explanation: Know the main parts of a PC and their purposes.

payload.template: First identify the problem by asking the user. Next check the {{blank:a}} causes, and test one possible cause at a time. When the fault is fixed, {{blank:b}} that the whole system works. Finally, {{blank:c}} the fault and the solution in a log.

explanation: Identify → simple causes → one change at a time → fix → test → record.
hints: Begin by finding out what happened; end by recording it.

stem: A technician cleans the 36 computers in a laboratory during the holidays. Each takes 15 minutes. How many hours does the job take? Give your answer in hours.
Give the abbreviation for the device that keeps a computer running for a short time during a power cut, so work can be saved.
explanation: An uninterruptible power supply (UPS) has a battery that takes over during a power cut.

stem: Describe **four** preventive maintenance tasks for a school computer laboratory. [4]

points.description: Clean dust from fans, vents, keyboards and mice regularly (prevents overheating/faults)
Use surge protectors / a UPS to protect against power surges and cuts
Install operating system/software updates and keep antivirus up to date
Make regular backups / run disk clean-up or defragment HDDs / keep the room cool and dry

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Clean dust from fans and keyboards each term; connect the computers through surge protectors and a UPS; install updates and keep antivirus up to date; back up the shared files every week.

hints: Think about dust, power, software and data.

stem: A computer in a school library in Kwekwe beeps at start-up and will not load the operating system. The technician suspects the RAM.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State **three** safety precautions the technician should take before working inside the computer.

points.description: Switch off and unplug the computer
Wear an anti-static wrist strap / touch the metal case to discharge static
Hold components by their edges / keep new parts in anti-static bags / never open the PSU

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Switch off and unplug the computer; wear an anti-static wrist strap; hold the RAM module by its edges.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Describe how the technician should find and fix the fault.

points.description: Remove the RAM module and reseat it firmly until the clips lock, then test
If the fault remains, test the module in another slot / test with a known working module (or run a memory diagnostic)
Replace the faulty module (or report a faulty slot), then test and record the fix

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Reseat the RAM firmly and restart. If it still beeps, try the module in another slot or swap in a module known to work, to find whether the module or slot is faulty. Replace the faulty module, test the computer and record the repair in the log.

explanation: Unplug, prevent static, handle by edges; reseat, test one change at a time, replace, record.
hints: Safety precautions first, then the steps to replace the part.

stem: Form 4 pupils at a school in Chinhoyi are assembling a PC from new parts.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Which part should be fitted onto the CPU straight after it is placed in its socket?

options.content: The keyboard and mouse cables
options.rationale: Peripherals are connected last.

options.content: The heat sink and fan (with thermal paste)
options.rationale: Correct: the CPU must be cooled.

options.content: The monitor and its video cable
options.rationale: Peripherals are connected last.

options.content: The side panel of the case
options.rationale: The case is closed at the end.

parts.explanation: Thermal paste, then the heat sink and fan.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Describe the remaining steps to complete the assembly after the CPU and its cooler are fitted.

points.description: Fit the RAM into its slots and fix the motherboard into the case
Install the PSU, storage drive(s) and any expansion cards
Connect power, data and front-panel cables, close the case, connect peripherals and test (POST)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Push the RAM into its slots, then screw the motherboard into the case. Fit the PSU, the drive and any expansion cards, connect the power, data and front-panel cables, close the case, plug in the monitor, keyboard and mouse and switch on to check the POST.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: When switched on, the PC shows "no boot device". Give **two** possible causes.

points.description: The storage drive's data or power cable is loose / not connected
No operating system has been installed yet / the drive is faulty or not detected

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The drive's data or power cable may not be connected, or no operating system has been installed on the new drive.

explanation: Cooler after the CPU; RAM, motherboard, PSU, drives, cables, test; a no-boot-device message points to cables or a missing OS.
hints: Assemble from the motherboard outwards, then the case, PSU and drives.
